title: White Label Call Tracking for Pay Per Call Networks
h1: White label call tracking for pay-per-call networks
description: White label call tracking explained for pay-per-call networks: what affiliate and buyer portals should show, and questions to ask before you choose.
faq: What is white label call tracking?

It is call tracking software that a network can offer to its affiliates and buyers under its own brand. Partners log in to see their calls, earnings or charges, while the tracking and routing run on the platform behind the scenes.
Why do pay per call networks use white label portals?

Branded portals let affiliates and buyers check their own call records and download statements, which reduces payout disputes and manual reporting and keeps partners working with the network directly.
What should a call buyer portal include?
At a minimum: every call delivered with duration and billable status, recordings or transcripts where enabled, the buyer's caps and hours, and downloadable statements that match the invoice.
body:
White label call tracking lets a pay-per-call network give its affiliates and call buyers their own logins to see calls, earnings and statements, under the network's brand instead of the software vendor's. The tracking, routing and reporting run on the platform behind the scenes; your partners only see your network. It matters because the portal is where partners check whether they were paid fairly, so it becomes part of your product.

Why networks want white label call tracking

A network sits between the people who generate calls and the businesses that buy them. Both sides want proof. Affiliates want to see every call they sent and what it earned. Buyers want to see every call they were billed for, how long it lasted and why it counted. If you answer those questions with spreadsheets and screenshots, every payout turns into a conversation.

A branded portal fixes three problems at once:

  • Trust. Partners see the same call records you see, so disputes start from shared facts.
  • Time. Fewer "can you send me last week's numbers?" emails, because partners can look for themselves and download statements.
  • Relationships. Partners log in to your network, not to a third-party tool they could contact directly.

What a white label portal should show affiliates

Affiliates care about one thing first: getting credited for the calls they drove. Their view should include:

  • Their own tracking numbers and the campaigns each number belongs to.
  • A call list with date, duration and whether the call was payable.
  • Their payout rate and earnings for each campaign, so a different rate for a different partner is never confusing.
  • Downloadable statements for any period.
  • A quality view, so they learn early if a traffic source is sending too many short calls.

Our guide to pay per call affiliate payouts explains how to turn this data into automatic payments, and call tracking for affiliates covers what the affiliate side of tracking looks like.

What a white label portal should show call buyers

Buyers, such as insurance agencies, law firms and home services companies, need a different view. They want to know what they are paying for:

  • Every call delivered to them, with duration and billable status.
  • Recordings and, where switched on, transcripts with short summaries, so they can review call quality without listening to everything.
  • Their caps and hours, so they can see why calls stopped arriving at a certain point in the day.
  • Downloadable statements that match the invoice.

Each vertical has its own habits. If you serve a specific industry, see the guides for insurance, legal and home services pay per call, or browse the industries hub.

Questions to ask before choosing a white label platform

  1. Do partners see only their own data? An affiliate should never see another affiliate's calls or rates, and a buyer should never see what you pay your traffic sources.
  2. Do the numbers match everywhere? The call count in your dashboard, the affiliate portal and the buyer portal should come from the same records.
  3. Can you set rates per partner? Networks rarely pay every affiliate the same. Per-affiliate payout rates should be built in, not handled in a separate sheet.
  4. Is quality visible? Grading sources on real call history lets you act before a buyer complains.
  5. Is sign-in secure? Portals show money and caller data, so two-step sign-in should be available.
  6. Can it connect to your other systems? Webhooks and an API let you push call events into your CRM or billing tools.

How white label call tracking works in Insight Dial

Insight Dial is built for publishers and networks, so the partner portals are part of the core product rather than an add-on. Here is how the pieces fit together:

  1. Set up campaigns. Create a campaign with country and state targeting, then add buyers with hours, daily caps, state rules and blocked numbers. The guided setup checklist walks you through each step, and the test-call tool lets you check routing before live traffic.
  2. Add affiliates and buyers. Give each affiliate their own tracking numbers and payout rate. Dynamic number insertion shows the right number on each landing page, so every call is credited to the right source. See call tracking and routing.
  3. Turn on white-label portals. Affiliates and buyers sign in to portals under your brand to see their calls, earnings or charges, and download statements. Two-step sign-in is available. See payouts and portals.
  4. Watch quality. Every source gets a Good, Watch or Poor grade, and sources sending too many short calls can be paused automatically. See quality grades.
  5. Sell calls the way you want. Use waterfall routing, or real-time bidding where buyers are pinged in parallel and the highest bid above your minimum wins, with a fall-back if nobody bids.
  6. Stay informed. Send alerts to Slack, Discord, Teams or WhatsApp, and push call events to your own systems with signed webhooks and the open API.

Pricing is pay as you go: a per-minute call rate plus a monthly price per tracking number, taken from a topped-up balance. Quotes are available on request; see pricing for details.

Common mistakes when launching partner portals

  • Launching before rules are written down. A portal shows which calls were payable. If the rules for minimum duration, states and repeat callers were never agreed, the portal just shows the disagreement faster.
  • Sharing one number across sources. If two affiliates share a tracking number, no portal can tell them apart.
  • Skipping test calls. Place test calls for every buyer and check that they appear correctly in both portals before inviting partners.
  • Forgetting compliance. Recording notices and do-not-call handling help, but check your obligations for each state and vertical with your own counsel.
